question.explanation:
First, we find the first-order derivative $f_{y}(x,y,z)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{y}(x,y,z) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(e^{xyz}\right) \\[3pt] &=e^{x y z} \cdot xz\\[3pt] &=xz{e^{xyz}} \end{align*}

Now, we find $f_{yy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{y}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{yy}(x,y,z)&=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_{x}(x,y,z) \right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(\left(xz{e^{xyz}} \right)\right) \\[3pt] &=xze^{x y z} \cdot xz\\[3pt] &=x^2z^2e^{x y z} \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{yyx}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating $f_{yy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{yyx}(x,y,z) &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_{yy}(x,y,z) \right) \\[3pt] &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( x^2z^2e^{x y z} \right) \\[3pt] &=z^2\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left( x^2e^{x y z} \right) \\[3pt] &=z^2\left[ 2x\cdot e^{xyz}+ x^2e^{xyz}\cdot yz\right]\\[3pt] &=x z^{2} \left(2+x y z \right) e^{x y z} \end{align*}

Finally, we evaluate $f_{yyx}(x,y,z)$ at $(1,0,1)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{yyx}(1,0,1) &=1\cdot 1^{2}\cdot \left(2+1\cdot 0\cdot 1 \right)\cdot e^{1\cdot 0\cdot 1} = 1\cdot(2+0) \cdot e^0 =2 \end{align*}

question.text: For the function $f(x,y),$ calculate $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2}$ given that $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x} =2 x \cos{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right)}.$
question.explanation:
To find $\dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2}$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative $\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x}$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac {\partial^2 f }{\partial x^2} &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(\dfrac {\partial f}{\partial x} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\partial }{\partial x} \left(2 x \cos{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right) }\right)\\[5pt] &=2\cdot\cos{\left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right) }+ 2x\cdot \left(- \sin \left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right)\right)\cdot 2x\\[5pt] &= 2\cos \left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right)-4x^2\sin\left(x^{2} + y^{2} \right) \end{align*}

First, we find the first-order derivative $f_{y}(x,y)\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{y}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(\sin{(xy)} \right) \\[3pt] &=x\cos{(xy)} \end{align*}

Next, we find $f_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating $f_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{yy}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left(f_y(x,y) \right) \\[3pt] &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial y} \left( x\cos{(xy)} \right) \\[3pt] &=-x^2\sin{(xy)} \end{align*}

Finally, we find $f_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating $f_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} f_{yyx}(x,y) &= \dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(f_{yy} (x,y)\right) \\[3pt] &=\dfrac {\partial }{\partial x} \left(-x^2\sin{(xy)}\right) \\[3pt] &=-2x \cdot \sin{(xy)} -x^2\cdot \cos{(xy)} \cdot y\\[3pt] &=-2x\sin{(xy)} -x^2y\cos{(xy)} \end{align*}
